CA Bundle Tracker

Which software ships its own Certificate Authority (CA) trust store vs. trusting the host operating system's bundle? A reference for understanding patch propagation after CA compromises.

Why this matters

In October 2026, eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were found to have trivially weak private keys (integers as small as 4 on secp384r1). Every trust store containing these CAs needed patching.

Software that bundles its own CA certificates requires its own update — an OS-level patch does not reach it. Java applications, Python environments, Node.js runtimes, Docker images, and Electron apps each carry independent copies that may remain vulnerable long after the OS is patched.

No definitive public reference existed for mapping software to its CA trust source. This page fills that gap.

Bundled — ships own CA store, independent of OS
OS Store — delegates to the operating system
Fallback — OS primary, bundled fallback
Hybrid — own store + OS supplement

Scan Your System

The emudhra-scanner tool checks whether any compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs are still trusted on your machine.

cargo install --path scanner && emudhra-scanner

Cross-platform (Linux, macOS, Windows). Scans OS store, Java cacerts, Python certifi, Firefox/NSS, curl bundles, and more. Use --scan-binary <path> for any compiled binary.

Worst-case patch lag

Android devices on old OS versions may never receive the ca-certificates update. Carrier-locked phones on Android 12 and earlier are the longest tail.

Docker images built before the distrust and never rebuilt carry the compromised CAs indefinitely. Any containerized service that validates certificates against its baked-in bundle remains exposed.

Java applications deployed with a custom javax.net.ssl.trustStore pointing to a stale cacerts file will not benefit from a JDK upgrade.

Embedded / IoT devices that shipped with the eMudhra root in their firmware and receive no updates will trust the compromised intermediates permanently.

Compiled Rust binaries using webpki-roots have Mozilla roots baked in at compile time. Every deployed binary must be rebuilt with an updated crate version.

Data compiled from vendor documentation, source code, and post-eMudhra incident analysis (October 2026).
